 Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1.
Mr. Neeraj Garg and Mr. Rajendra Arya, learned counsel for the applicant.

2. Present application has been preferred by the applicants, who are husband and wife, under Section 528 of BNSS, 2023 challenging the proceedings of Criminal Case No. 531 of 2025 (State Vs.
Sanjay Singh Rawat and another) pending in the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Pauri Garhwal,
wherein applicants are facing the trial for the offences punishable under Section 406, 420 IPC,
Police Station - Laxman Jhula, District Pauri Garhwal, arising out of FIR dated 13.06.2024 bearing FIR No. 0040 of 2024.
3. Brief facts of the present case are that an agreement was entered in between the respondent no. 2 and the applicants on 05.04.2023 for selling of the land owned by the applicants but within the stipulated period the sale deed could not be executed, consequently on 20.02.2024, respondent no.
2 filed a suit for specific performance wherein notices have been issued to the applicants /
defendants and on interim order was passed on 20.02.2024 restraining the defendants / applicants not to create any third party interest over the suit property.

sentences.text: Thereafter, the applicants moved an application under Order 7 Rule 11 CPC for rejection of the plaint, which was rejected by the trial court, against which applicants have filed Civil Revision before this Court, which is pending consideration.

4. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that after filing of the suit for specific performance by respondent no. 2, he has lodged an FIR dated 13.06.2024 bearing FIR No. 0040 of 2024 at Police Station - Lakshman Jhula implicating the applicants and three others for the offences punishable under Section 406, 420 IPC and during the course of investigation, those three other persons have been exonerated and charge sheet has been filed against present applicants wherein the Magistrate took cognizance on 08.05.2025 and applicants have been summoned.
Now, being aggrieved with the cognizance order, the instant application under Section 528 BNSS, 2023 has been filed.

1 5. It is argued by the learned counsel for the applicant that present FIR lodged by the respondent no.
2 on 13.06.2024 bearing FIR No. 0040 of 2024 is nothing but glaring example of abuses of process of law, which is evident from the fact that for redressal of his grievance, respondent no. 2 already instituted a suit for specific performance bearing Civil Suit No. 09 of 2024.
He further submits that proceeding is bad in law since the charge sheet itself reveals that the dispute in between the parties are pending in civil suit.

6. Prima facie, it appears that initiation of criminal proceedings on the basis of FIR lodged by respondent no. 2 is an abuses of process of law particularly when respondent no. 2 himself instituted Civil Suit No. 09 of 2024 for specific performance which is pending for adjudication before Civil Judge (Sr. Div.), Kotdwar, Pauri Garhwal.
7. All these aspects require deep scrutiny.

8. Mr. Tumul K. Nailwal, learned AGA for the State accepts notice on behalf of respondent no. 1.
9.
Issue notice to respondent no. 2.
10. Steps be taken within a week.
11. Four weeks time is granted to the respondents to file counter affidavit.

Two weeks, thereafter, is granted to the applicants to file rejoinder affidavit.
12.
List in the last week of March, 2026.

13. Till the next date of listing, further proceedings of Criminal Case No. 531 of 2025 (State Vs.
Sanjay Singh Rawat and another) pending in the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Pauri Garhwal shall remain stayed.
